subject: Band delta accountability guide and sample evaluations
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Payscale Surveys <surveys@payscale.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Band delta accountability guide and sample evaluations

Team —

I'm consolidating the acceptance criteria and a lightweight ops checklist for how we translate level bands -> local bands during offer approvals. Goal is to reduce offer rework and provide a clear audit trail for hiring managers and recruiters. Two asks in this note:

1) Review the suggested accountability steps below and flag any missing control points.
2) Payscale, please attach the 90/50/10 percentile snapshot for Software Eng ICs by region so we can map deltas.

Suggested acceptance criteria (draft):
- Anchor selection: 1 example hire per level (senior, staff) from the last 12 months with closed offers and signed comp data; annotated with reason for anchor choice.
- Geo multiplier band: explicit multiplier range and rationale (market index source + date).
- Offer tolerance: max allowable deviation from anchored local midpoint (+/- %).
- Manager sign-off: hiring manager + recruiter approval recorded in the approval doc.
- Finance sanity check: expected run-rate delta and budget bucket tagged.
- Audit note: brief note in the candidate file explaining non-standard exceptions.

Operational checklist (for recruiters/comp ops):
- Pull market percentiles (Payscale/Equilar) for role and location.
- Choose anchor from recent hires, attach supporting offer sheet (redacted PII).
- Calculate local midpoint and tolerance.
- Confirm manager and finance approvals via Slack thread or HR approval flow.
- Upload final table to Drive and link in internal hiring tracker.

Why this matters: we've seen a few recent escalations where offers exceeded approved tolerance because anchor reasoning wasn't recorded. If we bake this into the offer kit, CS and Finance will have a faster path to approve exceptions.

Payscale — tagging you in case you can share the CSV snapshot.

Camila
Camila Reyes
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Band delta accountability guide and sample evaluations

Thanks Camila — this is great and pragmatic. A couple of quick notes from calibration:

- Anchor examples: prefer a pair (one recent external hire, one internal promotion) where possible; that helps show both market signal and internal precedent.
- Offer tolerance: suggest we codify two tolerance buckets: "standard" (+/-8% from midpoint) and "exception" (+/-8-20% with exec approval).
- Geo multipliers: include an explicit version field (e.g., v2026-09) so we can trace which market snapshot was used.

I've attached a short example doc with two anchor mockups and a sample sign-off table. Also added a one-line phrasing for candidate communication so recruiters can be consistent.

Attachments: anchor_examples_v1.pdf

Laura Bennett
VP, Talent
Redwood Inference

- Sample size: metro-level counts vary; we marked cells with n<25 as low confidence.

2) Tessa, from the hiring ops side, add the anchor pair requirement to the offer checklist and include a redaction checklist for PII.
3) Laura and I will review the Payscale CSV and mark low-confidence metros before we publish the final geo multipliers.

I'll create the approval template in the HR tracker and ping Finance for a quick FYI review. If you want, I'll also mirror the short candidate communication phrasing into the recruiter playbook.

Thanks — small but important change that should cut offer friction.
